sections.h2: What closing costs does a Michigan seller pay by law?
sections.html:
The costs set by statute are two deed taxes and a recording fee. The state deed tax is $3.75 on each $500 block of value, and a leftover partial block counts in full. The county deed tax is 55 cents on each block, except in the largest county class, where the board of commissioners may set a rate up to 75 cents.

Commissions, title insurance, attorney charges and prorated utilities come from your listing agreement and purchase contract, so they vary from sale to sale. The statutory items above do not.

sections.h2: How do you calculate the Michigan deed tax on a sale price?
sections.html:
Divide the stated value by $500, round up any fraction to the next whole unit, then multiply by each rate. A $200,000 sale has 400 units. The state tax is 400 times $3.75, or $1,500, and the county tax at 55 cents is 400 times $0.55, or $220, for a total of $1,720.

The instrument has to state the real property's full value, or carry an attached affidavit that does. When land and movable items such as equipment change hands together, only the land is taxed provided the two values are listed apart. Treasury writes the affidavit form for the state tax, and the State Tax Commission writes the one for the county tax.

sections.h2: Who owes the Michigan deed tax, and by what date?
sections.html:
MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor. Payment is made to the treasurer of the county containing the parcel, within 15 days after the deed is handed over. A closing attorney or escrow officer usually deducts the sum from your proceeds and remits it for you.

The purchase contract can move cost from one side to the other, so read each line of the settlement statement ahead of closing day. A buyer who pays the tax in the seller's place may also file the later refund request.

sections.h2: Which Michigan deeds escape the state tax?
sections.html:
MCL 207.526 names a long run of exempt instruments. These are the ones a house seller is most likely to meet:

  • A deed whose consideration is under $100.
  • A deed running from a parent to a son, daughter, stepchild or adopted child, and a deed running to a grandchild in any of those categories.
  • A spousal conveyance that sets up or dissolves a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A judgment or court order that directs a transfer and sets no dollar consideration.
  • A deed that results from a mortgage foreclosure or replaces one. A later resale by the foreclosing entity is taxed.
  • A corrective quitclaim that fixes a flaw in title the grantee already holds.
  • A land contract that keeps legal title with the vendor until full payment.

The county act, MCL 207.505, carries a similar list without the child and grandchild exemptions. Your closing agent should test the deed against both lists.

sections.h2: Can a Michigan seller recover deed tax already paid?
sections.html:
Sometimes. A seller, or a buyer who paid the tax in the seller's place, who believes the deed met an exemption on its signing date may apply to Treasury for money back. The refund right reaches transfers made in the four years before the amendment that created it.

One refund route is aimed at homeowners. Paragraph (u) of MCL 207.526 applies when the seller had claimed the principal residence exemption, the parcel's state equalized value had not risen above its value on the first tax day after occupancy or purchase (whichever came later), and the price was set by arm's length negotiation. Have your closing agent test the sale against that rule before the deed is signed.

sections.h2: What is the Michigan fee for recording a seller's deed?
sections.html:
MCL 600.2567 sets a flat $30 to record one document of any length. That one section also prices extras: $1 per page for copies, $5 to certify a recorded document, and a $5 floor on any records search at 50 cents per year searched.

A charter county can adopt a different schedule by ordinance or resolution, though it may not charge above its cost of providing the service. Phone the recording office for your parcel before mailing anything. An electronic filing must be paid for within one business day after the office receives it.

sections.h2: What do the deed taxes come to at several sale prices?
sections.html:
A few worked sales show how the block counting plays out in a county below the 2,000,000 population line, using the state rate and the 55-cent county rate:

  • $90,000 sale: 180 blocks. State $675, county $99, combined $774.
  • $125,000 sale: 250 blocks. State $937.50, county $137.50, combined $1,075.
  • $450,000 sale: 900 blocks. State $3,375, county $495, combined $3,870.
  • $200,250 sale: 401 blocks, because the extra $250 counts as a full block. State $1,503.75, county $220.55, combined $1,724.30.

Netting these against your payoff, commission and prorated bills gives a more realistic proceeds figure than the sale price alone. A seller whose deed is on the exempt list owes none of it, which can change the math on a family transfer.

sections.h2: How do land contracts and foreclosure sales change the costs?
sections.html:
Deed tax is waived on a land contract while the vendor keeps legal title until the price is fully paid (MCL 207.526(o)). Property tax runs the other way. A land contract signed after 1994 counts under MCL 211.27a(6)(b) as a change of ownership, which resets the taxable value in the following year. Recording the deed later does not reset it twice.

Paragraph (v) of the same section exempts a foreclosure deed or deed in lieu from the state tax, but not the foreclosing entity's own resale. A borrower behind on payments should ask the county treasurer how a chosen deed will be taxed before signing it.

sections.h2: What happens to property taxes when a Michigan house sells?
sections.html:
The grantee has 45 days to file a transfer notice with the local assessor, on a State Tax Commission form that shows the parties, date, actual price and parcel number. Separately, the recording office sends the assessor a list of recorded transfers at least once a month.

Under MCL 211.27a a change of ownership lifts the taxable value to full state equalized value from the following January. A transfer to a spouse does not trigger the reset, and since 2014 neither does a residential transfer to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild who keeps it non-commercial. The contract decides how this year's bill is split, and the settlement statement carries the proration line.

faqs.q: What would deed taxes total on a $300,000 Michigan sale?
faqs.a: Roughly $2,580 where the county has under 2,000,000 residents. Six hundred $500 units at $3.75 give $2,250, and at 55 cents they give $330 more.

faqs.q: Is the buyer or the seller responsible for the deed tax?
faqs.a: The statute names the seller, so the seller normally funds it out of proceeds. A purchase agreement may allocate it differently.

faqs.q: How much does Michigan charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: The statutory base is $30 per document, with certification priced separately. Charter counties may publish another schedule.

faqs.q: Does gifting the house to my daughter or son create deed tax?
faqs.a: Under MCL 207.526, paragraph (j) frees a deed to a son, daughter, stepchild or adopted child from the state tax, and paragraph (k) does the same for grandchildren. The county list in MCL 207.505 has no matching paragraph, so confirm the county side with the treasurer.

faqs.q: What is the payment deadline for the tax?
faqs.a: Fifteen days from delivery of the deed. Closing funds normally cover it.
